items.title: Evidence-State Rewards for Long-Context Reasoning
items.abstract: Long-context reasoning requires models to locate, revise, and synthesize evidence distributed across lengthy inputs. Existing long-context RL methods usually reward final answers or static evidence extraction, offering little feedback on how intermediate actions change the model's evidence state. We propose Maven, a reinforcement learning framework with an editable evidence memory. Maven defines an answer-conditioned evidence-state value and rewards action-level state transitions: add actions are credited by marginal gain and hindsight contribution, link actions by evidence synergy, and drop actions by improved answer support after removing misleading evidence. These rewards are assigned to the corresponding action spans in GRPO. Across Llama and Qwen models on LongBench v2, LongReason, and RULER, Maven outperforms outcome-only RL and evidence-identification baselines, producing more sufficient evidence sets and lower distractor retention. Our results show that long-context RL benefits from optimizing stateful evidence navigation rather than one-shot evidence extraction.

items.llm_tldr_en: Maven proposes a reinforcement learning framework with editable evidence memory, defining answer-conditioned evidence-state values and rewarding action-level state transitions for long-context reasoning.
items.llm_tldr_cn: 本文提出Maven，一种带有可编辑证据记忆的强化学习框架。通过定义答案条件下的证据状态值并对动作级状态转换（添加、链接、删除证据）进行奖励，有效引导模型在长上下文中定位和综合证据。在Llama和Qwen模型上的实验表明该方法提升了推理性能。
